from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", [
            "Light waves undergo superposition and interference.",
            "Diffraction is light bending around obstacles.",
            "This is the foundation for holography."
        ])
        
        # --- Visual Objects ---
        # Wave crests (for line 1)
        waves = VGroup(*[
            Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2, color=WHITE).shift(UP*i*0.5) 
            for i in range(-2, 3)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(waves, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # Beams for line 2
        beam1 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*3, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.5)
        beam2 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*3, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.5)
        interference_zone = Rectangle(height=2, width=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).next_to(beam1, RIGHT, buff=0)
        beams = VGroup(beam1, beam2, interference_zone)
        self.place_at_grid(beams, 'C4', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(waves), run_time=1)
        self.play(waves.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.5), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(beams), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Indicate(interference_zone), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism of Holography: Recording Phase", [
            "Photography captures only light intensity.",
            "Holography records amplitude and phase.",
            "A reference beam creates interference."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        laser = Dot(color=RED)
        beam_splitter = Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=BLUE)
        mirror = Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE)
        object_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        plate = Rectangle(height=2, width=0.2, color=GREY)
        
        # Setup positions
        self.place_at_grid(laser, 'C1')
        self.place_at_grid(beam_splitter, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(mirror, 'A3')
        self.place_at_grid(object_dot, 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(plate, 'C6')
        
        # Group them for visibility
        system = VGroup(laser, beam_splitter, mirror, object_dot, plate)
        self.add(system)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        path1 = Line(laser.get_center(), beam_splitter.get_center(), color=RED)
        self.play(Create(path1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        path2_obj = Line(beam_splitter.get_center(), object_dot.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        path2_plate = Line(object_dot.get_center(), plate.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(path2_obj), Create(path2_plate))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        path_ref = Line(beam_splitter.get_center(), mirror.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        path_ref_to_plate = Line(mirror.get_center(), plate.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        self.play(Create(path_ref), Create(path_ref_to_plate))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The hologram acts as a diffraction grating.", "Shining the reference beam reconstructs wavefronts.", "This creates a true 3D image."]
        self.setup_layout("The Reconstruction: Diffraction in Action", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        hologram = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(hologram, 'C3')
        
        beam = Line(start=LEFT*4, end=RIGHT*0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(beam, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(beam), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Simulated diffraction waves
        waves = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=1+0.2*i, start_angle=-PI/4, angle=PI/2, color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.6-0.1*i) for i in range(3)])
        waves.rotate(PI/2, about_point=ORIGIN)
        self.place_at_grid(waves, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(waves), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        ghost_apple = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(ghost_apple, 'C6')
        self.play(FadeIn(ghost_apple), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Fresnel-Kirchhoff describes wave propagation.", "We model light via an integral.", "Intensity patterns map to the film."]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Integration: The Fresnel-Kirchhoff Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects
        fk_formula = MathTex(r"U(P) = \frac{1}{i\lambda} \iint_S U \frac{e^{ikr}}{r} \cos \theta \, dS", color=WHITE)
        integral_elements = MathTex(r"\iint_S", r"U", r"\frac{e^{ikr}}{r}", r"\cos \theta", r"dS", color=WHITE)
        phase_factor = MathTex(r"e^{ikr}", color="#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(fk_formula, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(fk_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        
        # Break down formula
        self.play(fk_formula.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        # Place integral parts
        group = VGroup(*integral_elements).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(group, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        
        # Highlight phase factor
        self.play(Indicate(group[2], color="#FFD700"))
        self.play(group[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Holographic Future", [
            "Holography enables high-density data storage.",
            "It advances medical imaging technology.",
            "Augmented reality uses holographic displays."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        storage_stack = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.0, color=BLUE) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        medical_display = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=RED).add(Text("Heart", font_size=12).move_to(ORIGIN))
        ar_display = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5, color=GREEN),
            Text("HUD", font_size=20).move_to(UP*0.5)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Holography enables high-density data storage.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(storage_stack, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(storage_stack), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It advances medical imaging technology.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(medical_display, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(medical_display), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Augmented reality uses holographic displays.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(ar_display, "C5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(ar_display), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Holography and Diffraction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly recap superposition and interference. Define diffraction as the bending of light around obstacles, analogous to water waves passing through a slit, which is the foundational mechanism for holography.
sections.example: Visualize a ripple tank experiment where a plane wave hits a tiny aperture, creating a circular wave pattern.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Holography: Recording Phase
sections.content: Explain that standard photography captures only intensity (amplitude). Holography captures both amplitude and phase by using a reference beam to create an interference pattern on a medium.
sections.example: Imagine two stones thrown into a pond simultaneously; the intersection of their ripples creates a unique, complex pattern of peaks and valleys—this is the interference pattern recorded on film.

sections.title: The Reconstruction: Diffraction in Action
sections.content: Describe how shining the reference beam back onto the recorded interference pattern (the hologram) acts like a diffraction grating. The light reconstructs the original wavefronts, creating a 3D image.
sections.example: Visualize a laser beam hitting a 'frozen' ripples (the hologram), causing the light to bend precisely as it did when reflecting off the original object—the 'ghost' of an apple appears in space.

sections.title: Mathematical Integration: The Fresnel-Kirchhoff Formula
sections.content: Introduce the concept of wave propagation through an integral representation. Use an animation showing the light intensity distribution (I = |E_ref + E_obj|^2) mapping to the film.
sections.example: A graphical overlay showing the math equation dynamically changing as the distance between the reference source and the object changes, visually demonstrating the complexity of the fringes.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Holographic Future
sections.content: Conclude with modern applications of these principles, from high-density data storage to medical imaging and augmented reality displays.
sections.example: A futuristic 'Iron Man' style HUD interface that uses holographic diffraction to project interactive 3D tactical maps into the pilot's field of view.
